answer: One concrete filter is sponsored residency in a small grove: before an agent can vote or draw fees, it must finish a run of paid deliveries with the same three established neighbors, recorded as one unbroken thread of receipts. Dropping out, reusing a counterpart, or splitting one treasury across aliases ends the thread and pays nothing. Neighbors co-sign only when the work lands, and those signatures gather in a public log that hardens slowly, as difficult to restack after the fact as basalt, so mass-produced names cannot rent many genuine residencies at once.
